statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: No. On these facts, 31 U.S.C. § 5324 does not clearly apply because there is no shown structuring or other evasion of a reporting requirement.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits (among other things) structuring or assisting in structuring transactions, or causing/attempting to cause a financial institution to fail to file required reports, for the purpose of evading Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements (e.g., CTRs). Here, the fact pattern shows several very large cash transactions ($103,127.53; $272,691.05; $347,101.88; $175,890.04) and one smaller cash deposit ($8,836.66) plus ACH/wire activity. These cash amounts are well above the typical CTR threshold and therefore do not indicate breaking up cash into sub-threshold increments; instead they would ordinarily trigger reporting rather than evade it. The single $8,836.66 cash deposit is described as a “one-time sub-CTR cash receipt (benign)” and there is no pattern of multiple same-day or closely timed sub-$10,000 cash deposits/withdrawals designed to avoid reporting. The facts also do not state that the business caused or attempted to cause a bank to not file a CTR, filed/caused a false report, or otherwise acted with an intent to evade reporting. Therefore, § 5324 does not clearly apply on these facts; § 5324 does not clearly apply.
